text:
Alex Ovechkin got "hot stick" cigars from the Lightning, per NHL.com, before what was billed as his final game in Tampa. The game itself belonged to a kid at the very start of his career and a former Capital who knows that building well from the other bench. Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal 2:11 in, John Carlson, a Capitals draft pick in 2008 and now a Lightning defenseman, had three assists against his old team, and Tampa won 5-2.

O'Reilly's goal came off what Sportsnet called a beautiful pass from Jeffrey Viel, and it set the tone for a first period the Lightning controlled. Charle-Edouard D'Astous made it 2-0 at 10:36 and Jake Guentzel 3-0 at 13:11 on a shot with a 5% chance of going in, the least likely goal of the night. Three goals, three different kinds of contributor: the 32nd pick of the 2024 draft, a defenseman jumping into the rush, and a winger who simply scores. Alex Tuch got one back for Washington late in the period.

Guentzel's second, a tip-in at 11:34 of the second off Carlson and Nikita Kucherov, came in a period Tampa owned, 1.21 to 0.38 in expected goals (the quality of the chances). Kucherov finished with two assists in a fortnight when the trade-rumour headlines have kept insisting the Lightning won't move him, and there was no sign of a player with his mind elsewhere.

Washington had the better of the third, 1.03 to 0.63, and Ryan Leonard, set up by Tom Wilson, made it 4-2 at 4:53. Andrei Vasilevskiy shut the door from there, finishing with 25 saves, a quarter-goal better than expected, and Anthony Cirelli's unassisted backhand at 17:19 ended it. Logan Thompson allowed four on 24, about a goal more than the shots deserved, and overall our replays gave Tampa the win 61% of the time.

The one worry for the Lightning: Daily Faceoff reported that Zemgus Girgensons left the game with an injury, on the same day Brayden Point came back off injured reserve and Conor Geekie went on it.
headline: Ovechkin's last Tampa visit belongs to O'Reilly and Carlson
